pins.title: Pack it on top
pins.sub: Blisters and scrapes happen mid-hike. Keep the kit where you can reach it without unpacking everything.

pins.title: Check it again
pins.sub: Mountain weather can change overnight. Look again at the trailhead, set a turnaround time and pack a rain layer.

pins.title: Light the tent, not faces
pins.sub: A bright beam blinds your friends. Hang a soft lantern for cooking and talking, and save the headlamp for the trail.

pins.title: Dew soaks you fast
pins.sub: Early trails are wet from the knees down. Quick-dry pants with a water-repellent finish shed dew and dry as you walk.

pins.title: Don't jump to 10
pins.sub: Add distance a little each week and train with the pack you'll carry. Feet and knees need time to catch up.

pins.title: Desert, but not warm
pins.sub: Bryce Canyon's rim sits above 8,000 ft (2,400 m). Expect snow, ice and cold, and check conditions on nps.gov.

pins.title: How much water to bring
items: Hot day or steep climb: 2 to 3 liters
Sip often, don't wait for thirst
pins.sub: Based on about half a liter (17 oz) per hour of moderate hiking.

pins.title: Know the distances
items: Bison, elk, all others: 25 yd (23 m)
If it moves because of you, you're too close
Use a zoom lens, not your feet
pins.sub: These are park rules. Check nps.gov/yell before you go.

pins.title: Pack a tiny repair kit
items: Duct tape wrapped on a pole
pins.sub: Enough to tape a boot sole or fix a strap and walk out.

pins.title: Not all are asleep
pins.sub: Many Smokies black bears den between late October and mid-December, but some stay active longer.
